To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Syp/SHPTP1D, a protein tyrosine-phosphate phosphatase, binds directly to the PDGF-receptor and to the GRB2/Sos complex and thereby links these two signaling pathways.
the PDGF receptor binds GRB 2-Sos indirectly via a 70-kDa phosphotyrosine-phosphatase, Syp.
Syp is the 70-kD protein that binds to GRB2 and that GRB2 binds to Syp via a YXNX sequence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of cell signaling and in particular the role of tyrosine phosphorylated proteins in the transduction of signals.
the mechanisms of growth factor signal transduction.
the molecular basis of signal transduction by growth factor receptors and the mechanisms of cell transformation by oncogenes and growth factors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phosphotyrosine binding (PTB) domain of GRB2 binds to phosphotyrosine residues in a YXNPXY sequence motif.
the Syp phosphatase acts as an adapter protein that binds to both the PDGF receptor (via the YXNX motif) and to the GRB2 complex (via the SH2 domain), thereby linking the two signaling pathways.
the PDGF receptor binds to the Syp phosphatase, which in turn binds the GRB2 adaptor, which binds the Sos guanine nucleotide exchange factor, which in turn activates Ras.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PDGF receptor interacts with GRB2-SOS via the SYP adaptor protein.
the PDGF receptor binds to the Syp phosphotyrosine binding (PTB) domain, and the Syp PTB domain binds to the SH2 domain of GRB2.
the PDGF receptor interacts with the GRB2 complex through the Syp phosphatase, and that the phosphatase activity of Syp is required to link the receptor and the GRBs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phosphotyrosine-binding (PTB) domain of GRB2 can bind to a phosphotyrosyl residue in a protein tyrosine-phosphate (PTP) that is associated with a receptor tyrosyl-phosphorylation site.
the PDGF receptor binds GRB-Sos through the adaptor protein SHP2.
Syp is a novel component of the PDGF signaling pathway.
